patients.label: 58-year-old Caucasian man with multiple myeloma who developed toxoplasma encephalitis after tandem autologous stem cell transplantation

identity_evidence.quote: We report the case of a 58-year-old Caucasian male presenting with toxoplasma encephalitis following tandem ASCT for myeloma

attribution_limitations: The discussion attributes the infection and the faint MRI enhancement to lymphopenia, corticosteroid effect, tandem transplantation and compromised immune recovery using hedged wording ("likely"); these are author interpretations, not recorded as facts.

Crystal nephropathy with renal failure is stated to have occurred while on sulfadiazine and the regimen was then changed; the source does not use causal wording, so no allergy or adverse-effect item is created.

The abstract describes subsequent therapy for progressive multiple myeloma while the case text describes ongoing maintenance chemotherapy; the source does not say whether these are the same treatment.
The dates for the two transplants are printed together ("June and September 2014, respectively"); the tandem transplant is kept as one procedure with that combined time.

The CSF result sentence is printed twice in the paragraph, first without units ("lymphocytes (62)") and then with units; both copies are treated as one CSF measurement. The cytology sentence, also printed twice, does not name its specimen.

In the negative workup sentence "CSF" explicitly qualifies the bacterial and fungal cultures; whether it also scopes the cryptococcal antigen and the viral PCRs is not stated, so their specimen is left empty.

claims.text: A 58-year-old Caucasian man was diagnosed with multiple myeloma in early 2014. He received induction chemotherapy with dexamethasone, cisplatin, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide and etoposide, pretransplant VDT-Mel chemotherapy with melphalan 200 mg/m^(2), and tandem autologous stem cell transplantation in June and September 2014. He was seropositive for T. gondii before transplant, and antimicrobial prophylaxis consisted of fluconazole, acyclovir and ciprofloxacin.

claims.text: He was neutropenic for about seven days after both transplants, with prolonged lymphopenia. Following engraftment on day +17 after the second transplant he developed low-grade fevers, headaches and impaired memory. MRI showed a new thalamic lesion with edema, mass effect and faint peripheral enhancement. CSF showed elevated protein, normal glucose and a lymphocyte-predominant WBC count of 94/µL; cytology showed no tumor cells, and blood cultures and the other infectious tests were negative. CSF and serum toxoplasma PCR were positive, establishing toxoplasma encephalitis.

claims.text: He was empirically started on sulfadiazine and pyrimethamine with leucovorin, developed crystal nephropathy with renal failure while on sulfadiazine, and was changed to clindamycin and pyrimethamine for 8 weeks. Response was favorable at 1-month follow-up. He was then switched to pyrimethamine, leucovorin and atovaquone as secondary prophylaxis during ongoing maintenance chemotherapy. The myeloma progressed, and he died 30 months after HSCT due to progressive myeloma with no evidence of toxoplasmosis.
